facts_of_case: Matrimonial discord between the parties. One FIR was registered against Kultar Singh for offences under Sections 406, 498-A, 323 IPC. He was acquitted. An application under Section 340 Cr.P.C. was filed by Kultar Singh seeking initiation of proceedings against Sarabjit Kaur on the ground that false evidence had been furnished by her.

legal_principles.principle: Parties are at liberty to move a fresh petition under Section 13-B of Hindu Marriage Act seeking dissolution of marriage by decree of divorce by mutual consent.
legal_principles.held: In view of the aforesaid statement made by petitioner's counsel, who is accompanied by the petitioner, the matter is adjourned to 15.10.2019.

legal_principles.principle: Parties would be at liberty to move application under Section 13-B(2) of Hindu Marriage Act for waiving of the mandatory cooling off period.
legal_principles.held: The parties would be at liberty to move application under Section 13-B(2) of Hindu Marriage Act for waiving of the mandatory cooling off period which shall be considered sympathetically by the Trial Court keeping in view the checkered history of the case.

outcome.final_order: The marriage is dissolved by way of a decree of divorce by mutual consent.

keywords: Latin maxim: Nemo judex in causa sua
use_for_drafting: appealing against Chief Judicial Magistrate's order
